answers.question: I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?
answers.answer:
No, you do not need to start from the beginning. Restart at the 8 x 2 minute level you were running in early October, and move on only when two sessions in a row feel comfortable.

The 5K on Sun Nov 15 is still possible, but running the whole way is a stretch from here. Running 5 km without a walk means about 38 minutes of continuous running at your current pace, and you are at about 18 minutes per session.

Check on Sat Oct 31. If you can run 15 minutes without a walk, with heart rate under 150 and no pain, keep the whole-way goal. If not, plan to run the race with a few short walk breaks.

new.analysis:
The week of Oct 12 was a full miss on running. All three planned walk-runs were skipped, and the four rest days were kept, so nothing was overrun. The only correction is that the planned running did not happen at all.

This is the second straight week with no running. Looking back, the week of Sep 14 went to plan, the weeks of Sep 21 and Oct 5 were skipped, and the week of Sep 28 was done. Three of the last five weeks had no running, so the pattern matters more than any single session.

The sessions you did run looked fine. Your walk-run average heart rate sat between 131 and 143, and pain stayed at 0/10. That means the base is still there after two weeks off.

Because of the break, the restart goes back to the 8 x 2 minute level you held in early October instead of picking up where the plan stopped. A full-volume return would load legs that have not run since Oct 3.

The Saturday session trades nine short runs for six longer ones with the same running time, about 18 minutes. Fewer breaks is the first step toward running without walking, and steady effort matters more than speed here.

At your run-block pace of about 7:40 per km, 5 km takes roughly 38 minutes without a break. You are at about 18 minutes of running per session now, so the gap is real. Three sessions a week for about three weeks is tight, and missed runs cut into that time, so do not double up on another day to make one up.

Your check-in describes a heavy family situation and sleep near 6 hours. When life is heavy, drop a session rather than squeeze it in, and keep Monday and Wednesday as the easy days they are meant to be.
